full_judgment:
6. Mr Mainul Hasan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that, the concerned authority is entitled to take action without assigning any reason and hearing in person as per BDR Ordinance, 1976 and there is no bar to take disciplinary action against the Government servant. He further submits that, any action taken under section 8 of the BDR Ordinance, 1976 cannot be challenged in any Court. Suits and legal proceedings are completely barred under section 9 of the BDR Ordinance, 1976. He finally submits that, after the decision of the Appellate Division in the case reported in 33 DLR (AD) 143, a member of the disciplined force cannot file writ petition before the High Court Division under Article 102(5) of the Constitution, as extension of such a privilege will undermine the discipline of the force which the High Court Division failed to appreciate the same and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed.
